title: Illuminating the Three Dogmas of Reinforcement Learning under Evolutionary Light
abstract: arXiv:2507.11482v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Artificial learning systems are graduating from passive learners to increasingly autonomous agents, lending pragmatic urgency to the question of what constitutes agency. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers arguably the most explicit formulation of agent-environment interaction, built on three core tenets: the environment as a Markov decision process, learning as policy optimization, and the agent as a maximizer of scalar reward. Recent work has called to revise these tenets: reconceptualizing learning as adaptation rather than optimization, broadening goals beyond scalar reward, and noting the absence of a formal theory of the agent in a formalism that so heavily emphasizes the environment. We argue that the artificial life community is uniquely positioned to illuminate this critique and concretize an alternative. We draw on open-ended novelty search as a complementary model of adaptation and goal-directed behavior beyond reward optim

translated_title: 在进化之光下揭示强化学习的三大教条
translated_abstract: arXiv:2507.11482v5 公告类型：替换 摘要：人工学习系统正从被动学习者逐渐转变为越来越自主的代理，这使得“什么构成代理性”这一问题具有了现实紧迫性。强化学习（RL）可以说提供了代理-环境交互最明确的表述，它建立在三个核心信条之上：环境作为马尔可夫决策过程、学习作为策略优化、以及代理作为标量奖励的最大化者。最近的研究呼吁修订这些信条：将学习重新概念化为适应而非优化，将目标扩展到标量奖励之外，并指出在一个如此强调环境的形式体系中缺乏代理的正式理论。我们认为，人工生命社区在阐明这一批评并具体化替代方案方面具有独特优势。我们借鉴开放式新奇搜索作为适应和超越奖励优化的目标导向行为的补充模型。
tldr: 本文从人工生命视角批判强化学习的三大教条，并提出开放式新奇搜索作为超越奖励优化的替代适应模型。
en_tdlr: This paper critiques the three dogmas of reinforcement learning from an artificial life perspective and proposes open-ended novelty search as an alternative adaptation model beyond reward optimization.
